In mathematics, the '''Askey–Gasper inequality''' is an inequality for [[Jacobi polynomial]]s proved by {{harvs|txt| first=Richard| last=Askey| authorlink=Richard Askey|first2=George|last2=Gasper|author2-link=George Gasper|year=1976}}<ref>{{Citation |last1=Askey |first1=Richard |title=Positive Jacobi polynomial sums. II |journal=[[American Journal of Mathematics]] |volume=98 |issue=3 |pages=709–737 |year=1976 |doi=10.2307/2373813 |issn=0002-9327 |jstor=2373813 |mr=0430358 |last2=Gasper |first2=George |author1-link=Richard Askey}}</ref> and used in the proof of the [[Bieberbach conjecture]].

==Statement==
For <math>\beta\geq 0</math> and <math>-1\leq x\leq 1</math>,

:<math>\sum_{k=0}^n \frac{P_k^{(\alpha,\beta)}(x)}{P_k^{(\beta,\alpha)}(1)} \ge 0</math> [[if and only if]]  <math>\alpha+\beta\geq -2</math>,

where <math>P_k^{(\alpha,\beta)}(x)</math> is a Jacobi polynomial.

The case when <math>\beta=0</math> can also be written as

:<math>{}_3F_2 \left (-n,n+\alpha+2,\tfrac{1}{2}(\alpha+1);\tfrac{1}{2}(\alpha+3),\alpha+1;t \right)>0, \qquad 0\leq t<1, \quad \alpha>-1.</math>

In this form, with {{mvar|α}} a non-negative integer, the inequality was used by [[Louis de Branges]] in his proof of the [[de Branges's theorem|Bieberbach conjecture]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=de Branges |first1=Louis |title=A proof of the Bieberbach conjecture |journal=Acta Mathematica |date=1985 |volume=154 |issue=1-2 |pages=137-152 |doi=10.1007/BF02392821 |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/acta-mathematica/volume-154/issue-1-2/A-proof-of-the-Bieberbach-conjecture/10.1007/BF02392821.full |access-date=17 March 2026|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Proof==
Ekhad gave a short proof of this inequality in 1993,<ref>{{Citation |last1=Ekhad |first1=Shalosh B. |title=A short, elementary, and easy, WZ proof of the Askey-Gasper inequality that was used by de Branges in his proof of the Bieberbach conjecture |journal=[[Theoretical Computer Science (journal)|Theoretical Computer Science]] |volume=117 |issue=1 |pages=199–202 |year=1993 |editor1-last=Delest |editor1-first=M. |series=[[International Conference on Formal Power Series and Algebraic Combinatorics|Conference on Formal Power Series and Algebraic Combinatorics]] (Bordeaux, 1991) |doi=10.1016/0304-3975(93)90313-I |issn=0304-3975 |mr=1235178 |editor2-last=Jacob |editor2-first=G. |editor3-last=Leroux |editor3-first=P. |doi-access=free}}</ref> by combining the identity

:<math>\begin{align}
&\frac{(\alpha+2)_n}{n!}\times {}_3F_2 \left (-n,n+\alpha+2,\tfrac{1}{2}(\alpha+1);\tfrac{1}{2}(\alpha+3),\alpha+1;t \right)\\
=&\sum_{j} \frac{\left(\tfrac{1}{2} \right)_j\left (\tfrac{\alpha}{2}+1 \right )_{n-j} \left (\tfrac{\alpha}{2}+\tfrac{3}{2} \right )_{n-2j}(\alpha+1)_{n-2j}}{j!\left (\tfrac{\alpha}{2}+\tfrac{3}{2} \right )_{n-j}\left (\tfrac{\alpha}{2}+\tfrac{1}{2} \right )_{n-2j}(n-2j)!} \times {}_3F_2\left (-n+2j,n-2j+\alpha+1,\tfrac{1}{2}(\alpha+1);\tfrac{1}{2}(\alpha+2),\alpha+1;t \right )
\end{align}</math>

with the [[Clausen inequality]].

==Generalizations==
Gasper and Rahman (2004)<ref>{{Citation |last1=Gasper |first1=George |title=Basic hypergeometric series |volume=96 |year=2004 |series=Encyclopedia of Mathematics and its Applications |edition=2nd |publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] |isbn=978-0-521-83357-8 |mr=2128719 |last2=Rahman |first2=Mizan}}</ref> give some generalizations of the Askey–Gasper inequality to [[basic hypergeometric series]].
